case: M/s G.R. Infra Projects Limited, Ratlam v. State of Madhya Pradesh & Ors.
headline: A GST Notice Can't Invoke the Extended Limitation Period by Merely Reciting the Word 'Fraud': Supreme Court
summary: The Supreme Court set aside a Section 74 CGST/MPGST show cause notice issued for AY 2018-19, holding that beyond a bare assertion of 'fraud or concealment of facts' the notice disclosed no underlying facts or circumstances from which fraud, wilful misstatement or suppression could be inferred. case: ADV Industrial Services Pvt. Ltd. v. Union of India & Ors.
headline: A Sanctioned GST Refund Can't Be Withheld Merely Because the Department Plans to Appeal
summary: The GST refund authority declined to release a Rs. 19.33 crore ITC refund that an appellate authority had already sanctioned, on the ground that the Department intended to challenge the appellate order. case: Aarem Insights Pvt. Ltd. (Formerly Shop CJ Network Pvt. Ltd.) v. Joint Commissioner of State Tax (Appeals)-VII & Ors.

summary: The petitioner had deposited Rs. 31,99,174 as statutory pre-deposit while appealing an MVAT demand of over Rs. 6.2 crore for AY 2016-17, and subsequently underwent CIRP, with its Resolution Plan approved by the NCLT on a 'clean slate' basis in March 2023. case: Manash Ghosh v. Assistant Commissioner of Revenue, Baharampur Charge & Ors.

summary: The petitioner's GSTR-3B returns for April 2018 to March 2019 were filed belatedly but before 30 November 2021, and Input Tax Credit was denied for the delay under a Section 73 adjudication order confirming a ₹1.18 crore GST demand. case: Welspring Universal v. Additional Commissioner of Central GST

summary: Justices Anil Kshetarpal and Shail Jain quashed a demand confirming recovery of a Rs. 76.72 lakh CENVAT credit refund (Order-in-Original dated 24.03.2025, arising from a Show Cause Notice dated 10.12.2019), holding that the Additional Commissioner could not ignore a subsequent CESTAT order that had expressly upheld the petitioner's entitlement to the refund under Rule 5 of the CENVAT Credit Rules, 2004. summary: An advocate enrolled with the Bar Council of Delhi since 1995, who separately qualified as an Insolvency Professional in 2017, challenged IBBI's clarification that his insolvency and receivership work was liable to GST under the forward charge mechanism rather than the reverse charge mechanism available for legal services rendered by advocates. case: Principal Commissioner of Income Tax v. Samsung India Electronics Pvt. Ltd.
headline: Revenue's Own Delay Sinks Its Transfer Pricing Appeal Against Samsung India's Royalty Payments
summary: The Income Tax Department's Special Leave Petitions challenging a Delhi High Court ruling on transfer pricing adjustments to Samsung India's royalty payments to Samsung Korea were dismissed by the Supreme Court on account of unexplained delays of 609 and 457 days in filing, with the substantive questions of law left open for a future case.

case: Termico Engineers & Erectors Pvt. Ltd. v. Deputy Commissioner of Revenue, State Tax, Baharampur Charge & Ors.

summary: The tax department suspended Termico's GST registration and issued a show cause notice proposing cancellation over an alleged ITC mismatch exceeding Rs. 8.04 crore across three financial years, without first verifying the supplier details and documents the taxpayer had already furnished. case: NTPC Ltd. v. West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company Ltd. & Ors.

summary: APTEL reinforced that force majeure clauses in power purchase and supply agreements must be construed strictly, holding they cannot be invoked to excuse non-performance where the triggering event was reasonably foreseeable or where the affected party failed to take adequate mitigating steps before and during the event.

summary: The Ministry of Mines has released draft rules clarifying the conditions under which a captive mine (one allotted to a specific end-use plant) may sell surplus mineral output in the open market following the amendment to the MMDR Act that permits such sale subject to payment of an additional charge, including the methodology for computing the additional charge and the reporting obligations a captive miner must meet b

case: Tata Power Company Ltd. v. Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam Ltd. & Ors. (Review Petition)

summary: Tata Power sought review of APTEL's own February 2026 judgment, arguing it had wrongly treated a key holding of the Damodar Valley Corporation ruling — that non-tariff disputes involving a generating company or distribution licensee fall outside Section 79(1)(f) of the Electricity Act and can be referred to arbitration — as a mere stray sentence. case: M/S Steag Energy Services (India) Pvt. Ltd. v. GSPC Pipavav Power Company Ltd.
headline: Judicial Restraint Reaffirmed in Reviewing Technical Evaluation of Infrastructure & EPC Tenders
summary: Reviewing an operation-and-maintenance contract dispute over a gas-based power plant, the Supreme Court set aside High Court interference and held that evaluation and award of complex, technically specialised infrastructure contracts falls within the domain of the procuring authority — judicial review is confined to illegality, mala fides or irrationality, not a re-run of the technical merits.

case: Sadguru Engineers and Allied Services v. National Highways Infrastructure Development Corporation Ltd.
headline: Delhi High Court Adjudicates Contractor Dispute Arising From a National Highway Infrastructure Contract
summary: The Delhi High Court dealt with a contractual dispute between a works contractor and the National Highways Infrastructure Development Corporation, part of a continuing line of Delhi HC rulings on EPC and works-contract disputes arising out of national highway and public infrastructure projects awarded and administered from Delhi.

case: Sai Consulting Engineers Pvt. Ltd. v. National Highways Authority of India & Ors.
headline: NHAI Can't Blacklist a Consultant for an Ordinary Contractual Breach Without Fraud or Collusion: Delhi High Court
summary: Justice Sachin Datta quashed NHAI's two-year debarment of consultancy firm Sai Consulting Engineers from future bids - imposed over alleged breaches of a 2018 consultancy agreement for Detailed Project Reports on several bypass/ring-road projects - holding that an ordinary contractual breach unaccompanied by fraud or collusion cannot justify blacklisting. case: U.P. State Highways Authority v. M/s Abhijeet Meerut Karnal Toll Road Limited

summary: A Division Bench partly allowed U.P. State Highways Authority's appeal against a 2017 arbitral award in a highway concession dispute, holding that a financial model based on assumptions cannot, by itself, quantify a claim for loss of profits, and set aside the Rs. 157.57 crore loss-of-profits component of the award while upholding the award's remaining findings, including the Rs. 25.53 crore award for EPC-contractor

case: M/s Coastal Waterworks Infra Pvt. Ltd. v. State Urban Development Authority
headline: Water Supply PPP Concessionaire's User Charge Revision Cannot Be Delayed Indefinitely by the Authority
summary: Hearing a suit under a bulk water supply PPP contract, the Delhi High Court directed the state urban development authority to process a long-pending, contractually due user-charge revision within eight weeks, holding that indefinite administrative delay in implementing an agreed revision formula defeats the commercial basis on which the PPP was structured.

case: Smart Urban Systems Ltd. v. City Smart City SPV Ltd. (Resolution Professional)
headline: Smart City SPV Governance Failures Do Not by Themselves Justify Bypassing the SPV's Board in Insolvency
summary: The NCLAT held that alleged governance lapses by a Smart City Special Purpose Vehicle's promoter-nominated directors, without a specific finding of fraud or diversion of funds, do not justify a resolution professional bypassing the SPV's board-approval process for ordinary operational decisions during the interim resolution period.

case: Backwater Infra Development Corp. v. State Pollution Control Board
headline: Environmental Clearance Conditions for an Infrastructure Project Cannot Be Relaxed Without Fresh Public Consultation
summary: The Kerala High Court quashed a state pollution control board order relaxing a key environmental clearance condition for an inland waterway infrastructure project without conducting fresh public consultation, holding that a material relaxation of clearance conditions is not a mere administrative modification and requires the same procedural safeguards as the original clearance process.

case: Konkan Railworks Infrastructure Ltd. v. Regional Railway Corporation
headline: A Railway Infrastructure PPP Concessionaire's Track-Access Rights Survive a Change in the Operating Railway Zone
summary: The Bombay High Court held that a private freight-corridor concessionaire's contractually granted track-access and priority-slot rights under a railway infrastructure PPP arrangement remain binding on the successor railway zone administration following an internal administrative reorganisation, rejecting the zone's argument that the reorganisation extinguished obligations undertaken by its predecessor.

case: Thar Infraprojects Ltd. v. State Public Works Department
headline: Defect Liability Period Does Not Extend Automatically Merely Because the Contractor Undertook Voluntary Repairs
summary: The Rajasthan High Court held that a contractor's voluntary rectification of minor defects during the defect liability period does not, by itself, extend the DLP or create a fresh limitation period for the employer to raise further defect claims; the DLP runs strictly per the contract's fixed duration unless expressly extended by mutual agreement.

case: National Highways Infrastructure Corridor Ltd. v. Bhargava Construction Co.
headline: Liquidated Damages for Delay in a Highway Construction Contract Must Be a Genuine Pre-Estimate, Not a Deterrent Penalty
summary: Applying Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 to a highway construction contract's delay liquidated damages clause, the Delhi High Court reduced the LD claimed by the employer, holding the clause's per-day rate bore no reasonable relationship to the employer's likely actual loss from delay and functioned instead as a punitive deterrent rather than a genuine pre-estimate.

case: Saurashtra Port Terminal Pvt. Ltd. v. Gujarat Maritime Board
headline: A Port Concessionaire's Cargo-Handling Exclusivity Cannot Be Diluted by Licensing a Competing Operator Mid-Term
summary: The Gujarat High Court restrained the Gujarat Maritime Board from licensing a second cargo-handling operator at a facility where the existing concessionaire held a contractually exclusive cargo-handling right for the balance of its concession term, holding that a port authority cannot dilute a negotiated exclusivity clause through a subsequent, separate licensing decision without first amending the existing concessio

case: Vindhya Highway Concessionaire Pvt. Ltd. v. National Highways Authority of India
headline: A Change of Scope Order Issued Without Independent Engineer Certification Is Not Automatically Void, But Compensation Must Still Follow the Contract Formula
summary: The Delhi High Court held that NHAI's change of scope order for additional service road works, issued without the contractually contemplated prior independent engineer assessment, was not void for that procedural lapse alone, but directed that the resulting cost and time compensation to the concessionaire must still be computed strictly per the concession agreement's change of scope formula, with a retrospective inde

case: Kaveri Canal Farmers' Association v. State Irrigation Department
headline: Irrigation Tribunal Directs Proportionate Canal-Water Allocation Where Upstream Diversion Left Tail-End Farmers Without Supply
summary: A state irrigation tribunal has directed the irrigation department to restore a proportionate, rotational canal-water release schedule after finding that unauthorised upstream diversion had left tail-end farmers in the command area without water for two consecutive cropping seasons, holding that registered water users at the tail end of a canal system hold an enforceable entitlement to their notified share.

case: Krishna Agro Equipment Financiers Ltd. v. Bhairon Singh
headline: Repossession of Financed Tractor During an Active Crop Season Set Aside for Non-Compliance With Notice Requirements
summary: The Debt Recovery Appellate Tribunal has set aside a financier's repossession of a farmer's tractor during an active sowing season, holding that the repossession agent failed to comply with the mandatory prior notice and fair-value inventory procedure required before taking possession of financed agricultural equipment.

case: In re: Simbhaoli Sugars Limited (Gursimran Kaur Mann v. Financial Creditor & Ors.)

case: X v. Y & Ors.
headline: 'Shared Household' Under the PWDVA Includes a Household the Woman Was Compelled to Leave Due to Violence
summary: Interpreting the definition of a 'shared household' under Section 2(s) of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, the Court held that a woman who was forced to leave a household due to domestic violence does not lose her right to claim residence in that household merely because she is not physically present there at the time of filing her application.

headline: Streedhan Can Be Quantified From Credible Circumstantial Evidence Even Without a Formal Inventory List
summary: Where a wife sought recovery of streedhan but had no formal, itemised list prepared at the time of marriage, the Court held that credible circumstantial evidence (including wedding photographs, family testimony, and receipts of purchases) can be relied upon to establish and quantify a streedhan claim, and the absence of a formal inventory is not fatal.

case: X v. Y
headline: Family Courts Directed to Standardise Video-Call Visitation Directions in Custody Orders
summary: Recognising the increasing use of virtual contact between a non-custodial parent and child, the Court directed family courts to consider including standard-form video-call visitation directions (specifying frequency, duration and platform) as a routine supplement to physical visitation in custody orders, particularly where parents live in different cities.

case: X & Ors. v. Y & Ors.
headline: Notional Partition Principle Reaffirmed for Computing a Deceased Coparcener's Share in an HUF
summary: In a partition suit involving a Hindu Undivided Family, the Court reaffirmed the notional partition principle: that for the purpose of computing the share of a deceased coparcener's heirs, a partition is deemed to have notionally taken place immediately before the coparcener's death, fixing shares as they would have stood at that moment.

case: X v. Y
headline: A Prenuptial Agreement Is Relevant Evidence of the Parties' Intent but Does Not Oust the Family Court's Jurisdiction Over Maintenance
summary: Considering a prenuptial agreement placed on record in a maintenance proceeding, the Court held that such an agreement can be treated as relevant evidence of the parties' financial understanding and intent at the time of marriage, but does not oust or conclusively bind the family court's independent jurisdiction to determine maintenance based on the actual facts and needs at the time of the dispute.
